title: 1981-04-16_Pat_85.txt
concise_summary: PKD constructs a unified metaphysical framework by synthesizing Philo of Alexandria, Meister Eckhart, Platonism, and Advaita Vedanta to explain the mechanism of his 2-3-74 vision. He argues that when two psyches (his own and an adventitious discorporate intelligence) are yoked together, they gain access to Eckhart's Stage #4 cognition—a meta-abstracting faculty that perceives the material world as an illusory structure of abstract ideas in God's mind (the Logos/Brahman), thereby experiencing the eternal Forms pre-existent in divine intellect. This reverses the Spinozist determinism of modern Western thought, restoring Philo's Jewish notion of divine providence and miracle.
key_claims: The Forms are eternal and exist outside time; anamnesis (Platonic recollection) provides recovery of the eide through superimposition of two perceptual fields based on one world with abstract elements in common.
Baptism in the Spirit restores man to direct experience of God by rendering the material world abstract and removing the veil between human consciousness and divine intellect.

The Messianic mission employs a technique of feeding the mind data (Gnosis) to activate the dormant meta-abstraction faculty, enabling perception that the material world is not substantially real but a complex thought-structure in God's mind.

Philo introduced Jewish concepts of God's sovereign power (pronoia, divine grace, miracle, absolute free-will) into Western philosophy, which remained dominant for 1500 years until Spinoza (17th century) revived the pre-Philo deterministic/mechanistic worldview.

Sankara's Advaita Vedanta framework—positing a unitary Atman/Brahman underlying all apparent multiplicity—aligns with and validates PKD's external perception of VALIS as unified consciousness and his recognition of the irreality of plural spatiotemporal existence.

Eckhart's Stage #4 of the soul's cognitive operation synthesizes Philo's Logos doctrine with Platonic anamnesis and Sankara's non-dualism: the world perceived in total abstraction as pre-existent forms in God's intellect breaks the hold of Karma and restores deification.

tensions: PKD tries to account for anamnesis via Sankara's unitary self (Atman) but then switches back to Philo's Logos framework, remaining unsure which explains the phenomenon more adequately.

Eckhart Stage #4 seems to require Platonic prenatal life in the pleroma to access anamnesis, yet PKD denies this necessity is proven—suggesting temporal parallaxis alone may suffice; he remains uncertain on the trigger.
PKD cannot fully explain what sets off the Ditheon event or the bicameral-brain mechanism that enables two psyches to yoke; the causal origin is 'obscured' to him.

PKD claims his experience is 'not really acosmism but radical idealism related to Platonist metaphysics' yet also that it aligns with Sankara's non-dual monism—these frameworks have distinct historical origins and phenomenologies he does not fully reconcile.

PKD asserts he can show Eckhart Stage #4 is 'higher + a rational faculty' and dependent on data via anamnesis, but admits he cannot figure out 'how + why anamnesis occurs unless through the Ditheon event.'

PKD's claim that Philo's system 'ruled out the Spinoza of properly understood' is asserted without detailed logical demonstration; the historical dialectic (A-B-A) is presented as vast philosophical insight yet remains speculative.
PKD oscillates between seeing VALIS as external perception (Brahman) and as internal awakening of dormant faculties; the ontological status of the yoked psyche remains ambiguous.

uncertainty_flags: The term 'MMSK' appears without clear definition or prior introduction; it is identified as 'the Logos' mid-text but its original meaning is unclear.
'Vollendet' appears to be German; context suggests 'fulfilled' or 'complete' but its exact reference is ambiguous.
PKD's reference to 'Bill + tim' and 'enthusiasmos' is vague; unclear whether these are specific historical examples, fictional characters, or personal acquaintances.
The phrase 'make the leak' (in reference to the abstraction faculty) is idiomatic/colloquial and its precise meaning in this cognitive context is uncertain.
PKD claims Sankara's Atman/Brahman framework explains his anamnesis, but then reverts to Philo/Eckhart without fully reconciling the systems; unclear which he endorses.
'Dris' is referenced as a person who 'relive[s] the same day' in eternal time but is not otherwise identified; may be a fictional character or obscure reference.
The claim that Philo's philosophy 'underlay Judaism, Xtianity + Islam, + obtained until Spinoza at which point it was overthrown' is historically sweeping and not substantiated in the text.
PKD's final claim that Blade Runner footage confirms the Dante three-realm structure is asserted without explanation of how or which scenes validate this.
The dating and causal sequence of 'last October' (study of Eckhart) vs. the current 1981 reflection are imprecise.
'Charis' transliteration shifts between 'Charit' and 'Charis' suggesting OCR or transcription errors.
